correctness.rationale: For every integer k>=2, odd-cycle uniqueness and one-change Cartesian geodesics establish all path claims. Empty-row extension and 1-1-1/2-1-1 occupancy arguments rule out maximal sets below five. Ten explicit geodesics prove the five-set is mutually visible; six disjoint exhaustive cases for every outside vertex supply a pair forced nonvisible upon addition. Standalone BFS checks agree at twelve odd lengths and exhaustively test sets of size <=4 for n=5,7,9; the mathematical proof, not the finite tests, handles all k.

originality.rationale: The exact minimum size of an inclusion-maximal ordinary mutual-visibility set in the odd toroidal family is not implied by published maximum-visibility formulas, by known lower formulas for two complete factors or path grids, or by the related high-girth connected-visibility results. The source introducing the lower invariant explicitly asks for toroidal-grid cases. Searches under equivalent C3=K3 product language and inspection of relevant primary text did not reveal the result. An unindexed stronger theorem remains a residual priority risk.

value.rationale: Brešar–Yero explicitly asks for the lower mutual-visibility number on toroidal grids (arXiv:2307.02951, concluding Problem 1). This gives the exact sharp value in an infinite natural fixed-width torus family rather than a finite special case. The five-vertex saturated configuration despite arbitrarily long odd circumference and the all-three-row obstruction expose genuine cycle geometry; neither follows from known Cartesian path-grid or complete-product values.
